title: Story of Aylan Shah and Abu Tammam
summary: Bakhtiyar recounted the story of King Aylan Shah of Khwarazm:
keywords: story of aylan shah and abu tammam
full_text:
Bakhtiyar recounted the story of King Aylan Shah of Khwarazm:

'King Aylan Shah had a wise and virtuous counselor named Abu Tammam, whose learning, honesty, and charity won the love of the entire nation. A jealous courtier named Qasim, burning with envy at Abu Tammam’s favor, resolved to destroy him.

Qasim approached the king and whispered falsely: "Sire, Abu Tammam boasts in private that your breath is foul and offensive; observe tomorrow when he approaches your throne: he will cover his mouth with his sleeve!"

Qasim then invited Abu Tammam to his home for dinner and served him a dish heavily seasoned with raw garlic.

The next morning, when Abu Tammam approached the throne to deliver state papers, he discreetly placed his sleeve before his mouth so that the smell of garlic would not offend the monarch.

The king, believing the slanderer’s accusation, wrote a royal order to the captain of the city fortress: "Strike off the head of the bearer of this letter immediately!" The king handed the sealed parchment to Abu Tammam, saying: "Deliver this to the captain."

As Abu Tammam left the palace, Qasim met him in the courtyard, saw the royal letter, and thinking it was an order for a rich gift of gold, seized it from Abu Tammam’s hand: "I will deliver it for you, brother!"

Qasim ran to the fortress, handed the letter to the captain, and was immediately seized and executed according to the royal decree!

When Abu Tammam appeared before the king the next day, the truth was brought to light. King Aylan Shah marveled at the divine justice that had made the slanderer carry his own death sentence, praising the virtue that shields the innocent.'
moral: The slanderer falls into the very trap he dug for the innocent, while truth is vindicated.
